blogPosts.content:
The Fundamentals of Percentage Calculations

Percentages express proportions as fractions of 100. Whether calculating retail discounts, inflation rates, investment returns, or exam scores, mastering percentage mathematics is an essential everyday skill.

Key Percentage Formulas

  • Percentage of a Number: (Percentage / 100) * Number
  • Percentage Increase: ((New Value - Original Value) / Original Value) * 100
  • Percentage Decrease: ((Original Value - New Value) / Original Value) * 100

Try the Free Calculator

blogPosts.content:
Understanding Body Mass Index (BMI)

Body Mass Index (BMI) is a standardized biometric screening tool developed by Adolphe Quetelet to assess body mass relative to height. While it does not measure body fat percentage directly, it provides a reliable statistical indicator of cardiovascular and metabolic health risk.

WHO BMI Weight Categories

Category BMI Range (kg/m²) Health Risk Profile
Underweight < 18.5 Nutritional deficiency risk
Normal Weight 18.5 – 24.9 Lowest disease risk
Overweight 25.0 – 29.9 Moderate cardiovascular risk
Obesity (Class I & II) 30.0+ High risk for hypertension & diabetes

Calculate your score instantly using our free BMI Calculator Tool.

blogPosts.title: How to Compress PDF Files Online Without Losing Quality (Step-by-Step Guide)
blogPosts.excerpt: Reduce PDF file sizes dramatically for email attachments, job portals, and university uploads while maintaining razor-sharp typography and image clarity.
blogPosts.metaTitle: How to Compress PDF Files Online Without Losing Quality (Step-by-Step Guide) | Mehzan Tools Hub
blogPosts.content:
Why Large PDF Files Cause Upload Failures

Whether you are submitting job applications, filing government tax returns, or attaching contracts to emails, strict attachment limits (often 2MB, 5MB, or 10MB) frequently block uploads. PDFs balloon in size primarily due to uncompressed scanned images, embedded TrueType/OpenType font files, and hidden document metadata.

How PDF Compression Works

Compressing a PDF does not mean degrading legibility. Modern PDF compression utilizes three distinct optimization techniques:

  • Image Downsampling: High-resolution 300 DPI scanner images are downsampled to a clean 150 DPI or 96 DPI web standard without visible pixelation.
  • Font Subset Truncation: Full 10MB font families are trimmed down to include only the exact glyphs and letters utilized in the text.
  • Metadata and XML Sanitization: Useless thumbnail streams, revision histories, and structural object overhead are stripped out.

Step-by-Step: How to Reduce PDF Size Online

  1. Open the Free PDF Compressor Tool.
  2. Drag and drop your PDF document or click Choose File.
  3. Select your desired compression intensity:
    • Low Compression (High Quality): Preserves 200+ DPI images for professional printing.
    • Medium Compression (Recommended): Perfect balance of crisp text and 70% file size reduction for email.
    • High Compression (Smallest Size): Maximum size reduction down to under 200KB-500KB for portal submissions.
  4. Click Compress PDF and instantly download your optimized document.

Comparison Table: Compression Presets & Target File Sizes

Preset Average Size Reduction Target Resolution Best Use Case
Extreme (Low Quality) 80% - 90% 72 DPI Govt exam portals & strict 200KB limits
Recommended (Medium) 60% - 75% 150 DPI Email attachments & client reports
Lossless (High Quality) 30% - 50% 300 DPI Commercial printing & legal contracts

Pro Tips for Managing Bulky Documents

If your PDF remains too large even after compression, consider removing unnecessary pages with our Split PDF Tool or converting heavy embedded bitmap diagrams into vector formats.
